title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization Project
summary: Hub of NIST's Post-Quantum Cryptography project, which leads the national and global effort to standardise cryptographic algorithms secure against future quantum computers.

title: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: NCCoE project translating PQC standards into practice, addressing the discovery of quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms in hardware, software and services in collaboration with industry.

title: What Is Post-Quantum Cryptography?
summary: NIST explainer describing post-quantum cryptography as a defence against potential cyberattacks from quantum computers and distinguishing it from quantum cryptography.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Project FAQs
summary: Frequently asked questions for NIST's PQC standardization project, covering technical implementation details such as acceptable key-pair and KeyGen seed formats.

title: New Draft White Paper: PQC Migration - Mappings to Risk Framework Documents
summary: NCCoE announcement of a draft white paper from its Migration to PQC project, a collaboration with industry, mapping post-quantum cryptography migration to risk-framework documents.

title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (NIST IR 8547, initial public draft)
summary: Initial public draft setting out the transition from quantum-vulnerable cryptographic algorithms to the three post-quantum cryptography standards NIST has released.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
summary: CISA initiative to unify and drive efforts with interagency and industry partners to address the threats posed by quantum computing to cryptography.

title: Product Categories for Technologies That Use Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
summary: Guidance identifying hardware and software product categories that currently support or are expected to support post-quantum cryptography standards, to aid PQC adoption.

title: Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: Joint CISA, NSA and NIST factsheet with recommendations to establish a Quantum-Readiness Roadmap and steps to prepare migration to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Post-Quantum Considerations for Operational Technology
summary: Examines the specific risks quantum computing could pose to industrial control systems and other operational technology, building on CISA's post-quantum migration work.

title: Strategy for Migrating to Automated Post-Quantum Cryptography Discovery and Inventory Tools
summary: CISA strategy for moving federal agencies to automated PQC discovery and inventory tooling, following OMB Memorandum M-23-02 on migrating to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Post-Quantum Cybersecurity Resources
summary: NSA resource page on post-quantum cybersecurity, including the agency's position on quantum key distribution and quantum-resistant algorithms for National Security Systems.

title: NSA's Cybersecurity Perspective on Post-Quantum Cryptography Algorithms
summary: States NSA CSD's position that it does not currently anticipate approving additional post-quantum cryptographic technologies for National Security Systems usage.

title: CSfC Post-Quantum Cryptography Guidance Addendum 1.0 (Draft 5)
summary: Draft addendum to the Commercial Solutions for Classified capability packages clarifying the usage of post-quantum cryptography technologies and product selections.

title: NSA Releases Future Quantum-Resistant (QR) Algorithm Requirements for National Security Systems (CNSA 2.0)
summary: Announces the Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0, algorithms analysed as secure against both classical and quantum computers that will eventually be required for National Security Systems.

title: Cybersecurity Speaker Series: Preparing for Post-Quantum
summary: NSA news highlight for a Cybersecurity Speaker Series episode on preparing for post-quantum cryptography; video content rather than a policy document.

title: Memorandum M-23-02: Migrating to Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: OMB memorandum describing preparatory steps federal agencies must take to begin their transition to PQC, starting with a prioritised cryptographic inventory.

title: Executive Order: Sustaining Select Efforts to Strengthen the Nation's Cybersecurity and Amending Executive Order 13694 and Executive Order 14144
summary: Executive order directing preparation for the transition to post-quantum cryptography, including agency-level actions due by December 1, 2025, once PQC products are widely available.

title: President Trump's Cyber Strategy for America
summary: National cyber strategy committing to promote the adoption of post-quantum cryptography and secure quantum computing, alongside securing the AI technology stack.

title: Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology (Report under EO 14178)
summary: White House digital assets report referencing NIST's post-quantum cryptography standardization project, launched in 2016 to solicit, evaluate and standardise quantum-resistant algorithms.

title: Memorandum M-25-34: Fiscal Year 2027 Administration Research and Development Budget Priorities and Cross-Cutting Actions
summary: OMB memorandum setting FY 2027 federal R&D budget priorities; surfaced in post-quantum cryptography search results but the candidate text shows no explicit PQC reference.

title: Report on Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: White House report describing how post-quantum cryptography addresses the security challenge posed by cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers through different mathematical algorithms.

title: National Cybersecurity Strategy Implementation Plan (Version 2)
summary: Second version of the National Cybersecurity Strategy implementation plan, including the initiative 'Prepare for Our Post-Quantum Future' and assessment of PQC impacts on the supply chain.

title: OFCIO Impact Report 2024
summary: OMB Office of the Federal CIO impact report noting initiating steps for federal agency migration to post-quantum cryptography and the establishment of an interagency PQC Migration Working Group.

title: Technical Design Choices for a U.S. Central Bank Digital Currency System
summary: White House technical analysis of design choices for a potential U.S. CBDC system, raising questions on how quantum computers would affect public-key cryptography and how the system would change post-quantum.

title: Playbook for Strengthening Cybersecurity in Federal Grant Programs
summary: Playbook for embedding cybersecurity in federal grant programs; its template material references post-quantum cryptography among mitigation measures, but PQC is not the document's subject.

title: 2024 Report on the Cybersecurity Posture of the United States
summary: Annual posture report describing federal engagement with stakeholders to prepare for a post-quantum future, including NIST's August 2023 submission of draft PQC standards for public comment.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: DHS guidance hub to help organisations prepare for the transition to post-quantum cryptography by identifying, prioritising and protecting potentially vulnerable data and systems.

title: Memorandum on Preparing for Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: DHS memorandum providing guidance to component heads to begin preparing the transition from current cryptography standards to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography Frequently Asked Questions
summary: FAQ document on post-quantum cryptography accompanying the DHS roadmap, noting NIST's plan to publish PQC standards in 2024.

title: Preparing for Post-Quantum Cryptography (Infographic)
summary: Infographic guide to help organisations create effective plans to ensure the continued security of essential data against the post-quantum threat.

title: Post Quantum Cybersecurity Standards Act (H.R. 3259, 119th Congress) - Bill Text
summary: Bill amending the National Quantum Initiative Act and the Cyber Security Research and Development Act to advance rapid deployment of post-quantum cybersecurity standards across the U.S. economy and support cryptography research at NIST and NSF.

title: Preparing Secrets for a Post-Quantum World - National Security Memorandum 10
summary: Congressional Research Service insight on National Security Memorandum 10, signed by President Biden on May 4, 2022, which directs U.S. preparation for the post-quantum transition.

title: S. 3312 (119th Congress) - Introduced Senate Bill
summary: Senate bill introduced in the first session of the 119th Congress, surfaced in post-quantum cryptography search results; the candidate text does not show its subject matter.

title: S. 2558 (119th Congress) - Introduced Senate Bill on Federal Quantum Migration Assessment
summary: Senate bill requiring the Subcommittee on the Economic and Security Implications of Quantum Information Science to assess possible migration by federal entities; explicit PQC wording not visible in the candidate text.

title: Science & Tech Spotlight: Securing Data for a Post-Quantum World
summary: GAO science and technology spotlight on post-quantum cryptography, the new encryption methods being developed and standardised to counter cryptographically relevant quantum computers.

title: Leadership Needed to Coordinate Cyber Threat Mitigation Strategy (GAO-25-108590)
summary: GAO report identifying central goals of the national quantum threat mitigation strategy, including standardising post-quantum cryptography, and noting the cost and challenge of migrating federal systems to PQC.

title: Future of Cybersecurity: Leadership Needed to Fully Define Quantum Threat Mitigation Strategy (GAO-25-107703)
summary: GAO report on quantum threat mitigation noting that OMB's Report on Post-Quantum Cryptography provided a migration cost estimate of $7.1 billion and reviewing how PQC standards documents were developed.

title: Executive Order: Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
summary: Presidential executive order (June 22, 2026) directing an accelerated nationwide migration to post-quantum cryptography, mandating that federal High Value Assets and high-impact systems transition to NIST-approved PQC standards (key establishment by end-2030, digital signatures by 2031) and tasking OMB, the National Cyber Director, NIST, NSA and CISA with implementation guidance.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Secures the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
summary: White House fact sheet accompanying the June 2026 executive order, summarising directives to lead an accelerated, nationwide migration to post-quantum cryptography and to deliver practical agency guidance on PQC migration including a cryptographic bill of materials.

title: FIPS 203: Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM)
summary: Finalised Federal Information Processing Standard (published August 13, 2024) specifying ML-KEM, a quantum-resistant key-encapsulation mechanism derived from CRYSTALS-KYBER and believed secure against adversaries possessing a quantum computer.

title: FIPS 204: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA)
summary: Finalised Federal Information Processing Standard (published August 13, 2024) specifying ML-DSA, a quantum-resistant digital signature algorithm derived from the CRYSTALS-Dilithium submission.

title: FIPS 205: Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard (SLH-DSA)
summary: Finalised Federal Information Processing Standard (published August 13, 2024) specifying SLH-DSA, a quantum-resistant stateless hash-based digital signature scheme derived from the SPHINCS+ submission.

title: NIST IR 8545: Status Report on the Fourth Round of the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization Process
summary: Final NIST internal report describing the evaluation and selection of fourth-round PQC key-establishment candidates (BIKE, Classic McEliece, HQC, SIKE) and announcing HQC as the only algorithm selected for standardisation to augment NIST's key-establishment portfolio.

title: NIST Selects HQC as Fifth Algorithm for Post-Quantum Encryption
summary: NIST news announcement (March 11, 2025) that HQC has been selected as a fifth algorithm for post-quantum encryption, to be standardised as a backup key-establishment mechanism alongside ML-KEM.

title: NIST Releases First 3 Finalized Post-Quantum Encryption Standards
summary: NIST news announcement (August 13, 2024) of the first three finalised post-quantum encryption standards (FIPS 203, 204 and 205), concluding an eight-year standardisation effort.

title: CISA Releases Product Categories List to Propel Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Pursuant to President Trump's Executive Order 14306
summary: CISA news announcement (January 23, 2026) of an initial list of product categories for technologies that use post-quantum cryptography standards, published with NSA pursuant to Executive Order 14306 to help organisations shape PQC migration strategies.

title: CISA Announces Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative
summary: CISA news announcement launching the Post-Quantum Cryptography Initiative to unify and drive efforts with interagency and industry partners to address the quantum threat to cryptography.

title: CISA, NSA and NIST Publish New Resource for Migrating to Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: Joint CISA, NSA and NIST news announcement of the Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography factsheet, urging organisations to develop quantum-readiness roadmaps and begin planning migration.

title: Frequently Asked Questions on Financial Sector Risks from Quantum Computing
summary: U.S. Treasury FAQ document explaining quantum-computing cybersecurity risks to the financial sector, including 'harvest now, decrypt later', and pointing financial entities to the NIST post-quantum cryptography FIPS standards (FIPS 203/204/205) for migration.

title: Harvest Now, Decrypt Later: Examining Post-Quantum Cryptography and the Data Privacy Risks for Distributed Ledger Networks (FEDS)
summary: Federal Reserve Finance and Economics Discussion Series (FEDS) working paper examining post-quantum cryptography and 'harvest now, decrypt later' data-privacy risks for distributed ledger networks; flagged for review as a FEDS paper reflects author research rather than official Board policy.

title: Preparing for the Post-Quantum Era: A Call to Action
summary: Joint CISA and G7 Cyber Security Working Group call to action published 3 September 2026, urging organisations and governments to begin transitioning to post-quantum cryptography. It sets out five priorities: raising awareness of quantum risk, developing national PQC strategies, advancing quantum-safe R&D, fostering public-private partnerships, and integrating PQC into cybersecurity requirements and procurement.

title: Treasury Announces the Quantum-Readiness Task Force
summary: Treasury press release of 24 August 2026 launching a public-private Financial Sector Quantum-Readiness Task Force to help the financial sector adopt post-quantum cryptography in an operationally resilient way. It runs three workstreams — sector alignment and PQC transition, third-party and vendor readiness, and digital assets and emerging technology risk — building on the G7 Cyber Expert Group PQC roadmap.

title: National Security Science and Technology Strategy (August 2026)
summary: White House OSTP strategy of August 2026 setting national-security science and technology priorities in support of the 2025 National Security Strategy, organised around four pillars and fourteen critical and emerging technology areas. It names post-quantum cryptography explicitly as a priority subfield under cyber and information technology, alongside a call to modernise cryptography and cyber infrastructure for resilience.

title: GSA Leads the Transition to Quantum-Resistant Technology
summary: GSA Office of Government-wide Policy post of 24 August 2026 setting out GSA's assigned responsibilities under OMB Memorandum M-26-15 for the government-wide PQC migration. It describes updating the Federal Identity, Credential and Access Management (FICAM) architecture for quantum-resistant algorithms, an interagency FICAM modernisation working group convened on 12 August 2026 with 40 participants from 17 agencies, and expansion of the FIPS 201 Evaluation Program PACS lab to test quantum-resistant solutions.

title: 2026 Post-Quantum Cryptography Summit (In Person, 16 September 2026)
summary: GSA-hosted federal Post-Quantum Cryptography Summit scheduled for 16 September 2026 in Washington DC, convening federal leaders, industry partners and subject-matter experts on PQC migration. The agenda covers federal migration strategy and marketplace dynamics, hands-on implementation guidance, and global threat analysis to accelerate agency quantum readiness.

title: NIST CSWP 39upd1: Considerations for Achieving Crypto Agility - Strategies and Practices
summary: Updated NIST cybersecurity white paper (update 1 issued 29 June 2026, superseding the December 2025 CSWP 39, which was formally withdrawn) surveying approaches to cryptographic agility. It frames crypto agility as a necessity rather than an option because the post-quantum cryptography transition has exposed the difficulty of swapping algorithms, and covers modularity, policy/mechanism separation and hybrid PQ/traditional mechanisms.

title: OMB Memorandum M-26-15: Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: Binding OMB memorandum signed by Director Russell T. Vought on 24 June 2026 implementing Executive Order 14412 and fulfilling OMB's duty under the Quantum Computing Cybersecurity Preparedness Act to direct agencies to prioritise critical IT for PQC migration and produce migration plans. It requires each agency to designate a PQC migration lead, sets a phased migration (Phase 1 strategy, planning and discovery over 2026-2027) and transition deadlines of 31 December 2030 and 31 December 2031 depending on use case; it does not apply to national security systems.

title: Executive Order 14413: Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation
summary: Executive order signed 22 June 2026 (companion to EO 14412) directing an update of the National Quantum Strategy, a national effort toward a scientifically useful quantum computer, quantum workforce development and domestic quantum supply chains. Section 4(f) directs the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of War to assess the national security implications of increasingly powerful commercial quantum computers, expressly including the implications for the migration to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Department of War Post Quantum Cryptography Strategy
summary: Department of War PQC Strategy, cleared for open publication on 16 April 2026 and announced by DoW CIO Kirsten Davies in June 2026, framing cryptographically relevant quantum computing as an existential threat to US military dominance. It directs an enterprise-wide migration to quantum-resistant cryptography on high-impact systems by 2030 and across the force by 2031, covering cryptographic inventory and discovery, PQC technology acceleration and testing, and revision of acquisition policy to use DoW purchasing power to drive commercial PQC adoption.

title: Securing Global Dominance: DoW Unleashes Quantum Defense Strategy to Harden Networks and Empower the Joint Force
summary: Department of War press release of June 2026 announcing publication of the DoW Post Quantum Cryptography Strategy. It summarises the department's plan to inventory vulnerable cryptography, field quantum-resistant cryptography on high-impact systems by 2030 and force-wide by 2031, and to use defence acquisition to accelerate the commercial PQC market.

title: Memorandum: Preparing for Migration to Post Quantum Cryptography
summary: Department of War CIO memorandum (dated 18 November) to senior Pentagon leadership, combatant commands and defence agencies requiring identification of PQC migration points of contact and a full cryptographic inventory across DoW information systems, including national security systems, weapons systems, cloud, mobile, IoT and operational technology. It prohibits procurement of non-CNSA 2.0 asymmetric PQC algorithms for key establishment after 31 December 2030 and requires phase-out of certain symmetric key distribution protocols by 31 December 2030 (31 December 2031 for solutions registered with NSA CSfC).

title: Working Drafts: Post-Quantum Cryptography Updates to the PIV Standards
summary: NIST news item of 12 June 2026 announcing initial working drafts of proposed updates to the Personal Identity Verification (PIV) standards to support post-quantum cryptography. The drafts identify the changes expected to be needed to use ML-DSA and ML-KEM with PIV credentials and are open for comment on a rolling basis.

title: PIV Standards and Guidelines - PQC Drafts (SP 800-73 Parts 1 and 2, SP 800-78, PQC Overview)
summary: NIST working-draft repository hosting the post-quantum updates to the PIV standards: a PQC Overview gap analysis plus draft SP 800-73 Part 1 (namespace, data model and representation), SP 800-73 Part 2 (card command interface) and SP 800-78 (cryptographic algorithms and key sizes). The drafts specify the use of ML-DSA and ML-KEM in the PIV environment, covering cryptographic identifiers, key formats, command behaviour and authentication mechanisms.

title: NIST IR 8610: Status Report on the Second Round of the Additional Digital Signature Schemes for the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization Process
summary: NIST internal report released 14 May 2026 describing the evaluation criteria and selection process for the second round of the additional post-quantum digital signature standardisation track. It announces nine candidates advancing to a third round expected to last about two years - FAEST, HAWK, MAYO, MQOM, QR-UOV, SDitH, SNOVA, SQIsign and UOV - intended to augment FIPS 204, FIPS 205, FIPS 186-5 and SP 800-208.

title: Nine Candidates Advance to the Third Round of the Additional Digital Signatures for the PQC Standardization Process
summary: NIST announcement of 14 May 2026 that nine algorithms have advanced to the third round of the additional post-quantum digital signature standardisation process, accompanying the release of NIST IR 8610. The additional signatures track seeks schemes with different mathematical foundations from the already-standardised ML-DSA and SLH-DSA.

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography: Additional Digital Signature Schemes
summary: NIST CSRC project page for the supplementary post-quantum digital signature standardisation track, running in parallel to the main PQC process and now in its third round. It hosts the round-3 candidate list, evaluation criteria and status reports for schemes intended to diversify the signature portfolio beyond the lattice- and hash-based FIPS 204 and FIPS 205 standards.

title: NIST SP 800-230 (Initial Public Draft): Additional SLH-DSA Parameter Sets for Limited Signature Use Cases
summary: Initial public draft released 13 April 2026 (comments closed 12 June 2026) specifying six additional SLH-DSA parameter sets at security levels 1, 3 and 5 as a technical extension to FIPS 205. The additional sets target limited-signature applications such as software and firmware signing that require faster verification and smaller post-quantum signatures.

title: H.R. 4942 (119th Congress) - Quantum Encryption Readiness and Resilience Act
summary: Bill introduced in the House on 8 August 2025 directing the Subcommittee on the Economic and Security Implications of Quantum Information Science to report on mitigating the cybersecurity and national security risks posed by cryptographically relevant quantum computers. Within one year of enactment it requires an assessment of US progress in adopting security measures including post-quantum cryptography, identification of the most vulnerable economic sectors, and a mitigation plan built on interagency and public-private collaboration.

title: S. 3597 (119th Congress) - National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act of 2026
summary: Bill introduced in the Senate on 8 January 2026 by Senator Young and colleagues reauthorising and extending the National Quantum Initiative through December 2034, and advanced unanimously by the Senate Commerce Committee. Among its provisions, grants awarded under the Act may cover reasonable costs of activities to adopt standards relating to post-quantum cryptography and to remediate quantum-related vulnerabilities.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group Releases Roadmap for Coordinating the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography in the Financial Sector
summary: Treasury press release of 12 January 2026 announcing the G7 Cyber Expert Group's roadmap guiding financial entities toward a coordinated transition to quantum-resistant encryption. The co-chairs frame quantum computers capable of breaking current encryption as a significant risk to the safety and soundness of the financial ecosystem, and the roadmap underpins Treasury's later Quantum-Readiness Task Force.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
issuingOrg: G7 Cyber Expert Group (hosted by U.S. Department of the Treasury)
summary: Roadmap document hosted on the US Treasury domain setting out coordinated steps for financial entities to plan and execute the transition to post-quantum cryptography, covering cryptographic discovery, risk assessment and third-party dependencies. Flagged for human review because the issuer is the G7 Cyber Expert Group, an international body co-chaired by Treasury, rather than a purely domestic US institution.

title: Post Quantum Cryptography Buyer's Guide
summary: GSA Federal Acquisition Service buyer's guide helping federal agencies acquire post-quantum cryptography capabilities, covering the NIST PQC standards, cryptographic inventory and assessment, and the contract vehicles available for PQC migration. It is the acquisition-side companion to GSA's PQC roadmap and to the government-wide migration directed by OMB.

title: Quantum Computing Cybersecurity Preparedness Act (Public Law 117-260)
summary: Public Law 117-260 of 21 December 2022 requires OMB to issue guidance within 180 days requiring federal agencies to inventory IT systems vulnerable to quantum decryption, with priorities set by OMB criteria, and to report those inventories every year. Within one year of NIST issuing post-quantum cryptography standards, OMB must require agencies to prioritise these systems for migration to PQC and to develop migration plans. OMB must also report to Congress on the migration strategy and funding. National security systems are exempt.

title: Getting Ready for Post-Quantum Cryptography: Exploring Challenges Associated with Adopting and Using Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms (NIST CSWP 15)
summary: NIST Cybersecurity White Paper 15, published 28 April 2021, introduces the challenges of adopting post-quantum cryptography once standardisation is complete. It discusses planning requirements for migration and NIST's next steps for helping with it.

title: FACT SHEET: Biden-Harris Administration Continues Work to Secure a Post-Quantum Cryptography Future
summary: White House OSTP fact sheet of 13 August 2024 marking NIST's release of the first post-quantum cryptography standards. It recaps administration actions: NSM-10 on post-quantum cryptography, OMB Memorandum M-23-02 setting migration steps for federal agencies (cryptographic inventory, prioritising critical systems), the July 2024 OMB PQC report, an OMB/OSTP roundtable with cryptographers, industry and agencies, and the 2023 National Cybersecurity Strategy.

title: Preparing Critical Infrastructure for Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: CISA alert of 24 August 2022 releasing guidance that helps critical infrastructure operators understand the quantum threat to the National Critical Functions. It urges organisations to inventory cryptographic systems, set acquisition policies and train staff for the transition to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Frequently Asked Questions about Post-Quantum Cryptography
summary: FAQ from the NCCoE Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography project documentation, last updated 30 June 2026. It covers the migration phases from awareness and inventory to execution, testing and validation, and gathers federal mandates, sector guidance and tools for organisations.

title: Memorandum M-26-16 (NSTM-5): Ushering in a New Golden Age of American Innovation: Fiscal Year 2028 Administration Research and Development Budget Priorities
summary: Joint OSTP and OMB memorandum of 21 July 2026 setting the administration's FY2028 research and development budget priorities for executive departments and agencies. Under mathematics and computer science, it asks agencies to prioritise foundational research that includes post-quantum cryptography.

title: Blockchain: Emerging Technology Offers Benefits for Some Applications but Faces Challenges (GAO-22-104625)
summary: GAO technology assessment for congressional requesters, March 2022, on the benefits and challenges of blockchain. In its section on long-term data security, it notes that quantum computers could in future break some of the public key encryption algorithms most blockchains use. It adds that federal agencies and academic researchers are developing post-quantum cryptography and that NIST is developing post-quantum cryptography standards.
